text: How do you get a navy past an unbreakable chain?
You take it for a walk.
Constantinople, spring of fourteen fifty-three. Twenty-one-year-old Sultan Mehmed the Second has the city surrounded.
kokoro: Constantinople, spring of fourteen fifty-three. Twenty-one-year-old Sultan Meh-med the Second has the city surrounded.
caption: Constantinople, spring of 1453. 21-year-old Sultan Mehmed II has the city surrounded.

text: But its harbor, the Golden Horn, is sealed by a massive iron chain, floating right across the entrance.
His fleet attacks it. And fails.
So Mehmed does something nobody sees coming.
kokoro: So Meh-med does something nobody sees coming.

text: His men lay a road of wooden planks over the hills behind Galata, and grease it with animal fat.
Then they drag the ships out of the sea. Around seventy of them. Up and over the hill.
caption: Then they drag the ships out of the sea. Around 70 of them. Up and over the hill.

text: Chroniclers say the sails were raised, and the rowers pulled their oars through the air.
On April twenty-second, the defenders wake up to an enemy fleet inside their own harbor. Behind the chain.
caption: On April 22, the defenders wake up to an enemy fleet inside their own harbor. Behind the chain.

text: Now the sea walls need guarding too, and a city already short on soldiers is stretched even thinner.
Five weeks later, on May twenty-ninth, Constantinople falls. And a thousand-year empire is gone.
caption: Five weeks later, on May 29, Constantinople falls. And a 1,000-year empire is gone.

text: All because one sultan took his navy for a walk.
